label: paragraph_title
text:
EUCHARISTIC CON-
GRESS.

label: text
text:
RELIGON ADDS TO NATIONAL
SECURITY

label: text
text: A HUGE SUCCESS.

label: text
text: Pierce Butler, associate justice of the supreme court of the United States, addressing the Eucharistic Congress last night, dwelt on the importance of religion as a force making for social stability and world peace.

label: text
text: "All that strengths religion, all that creates self respect, exalts the sanctity—of the home—and—the integrity of the family, adds to national security," said Justice Butler.

label: text
text:
Men only filled the stands for the candle light benediction services last night which began at dusk. More than 150,000 men gathered on Soldiers Field in the most solemn and most impressive picture of the congress. A light rain had ceased and a brilliant rainbow arched the east colonnade of the great stadium. Then came the solemn procession of cardinals and bishops and the great roll of voices joined in "The Divine Praise."
Thousands who were unable to gain admittance to the stadium heard the ceremonies through loud speakers. The ecclesiastical procession was more than a mile long.
The men's meeting was addressed by Cardinal O'Donnell of Ireland, and Cardinal Mundelein of Chicago celebrated pontifical mass. Three messages were received today from the Pope through Cardinal Gaspari, papal secretary of state, expressing joyous gratification at the success of the Eucharistic Congress.

label: text
text: The priests of the Eucharistic League will hold their 1927 meeting at Cleveland, Ohio, Bishop Joseph Schrembs of Cleveland continues as president of the league.

label: text
text: Almost 200,000 men filled the gigantic open air cathedral in the Soldier's Field. Memorial Stadium for the third general assembly and mass of the Eucharistic Congress. The first was the opening ceremony attended by all pilgrims and church officials and as many of the general public as could approach the stadium. The second was a service for women and the third, Tuesday night, for men only.

label: text
text: While the Sacred Host was lifted in benediction over the congregation, all those present, which included the greatest to the poorest, princes of the church and prelates down to the humblest pilgrim, made the sign of the cross with lighted candles. The altar was brilliantly lighted and the service was regarded as extraordinarily impressive.

label: paragraph_title
text: Pillgrimage to Mundelein.

label: text
text:
Thousands of persons already have started for Mundelein,�.named after Cardinal Mundelein of Chicago, which has become for the time being, at least, the American Holy City. A great procession is scheduled for Thursday and several hundred thousand persons are expected to make the trip to witness this event. Many pilgrims can be seen leaving Chicago equipped with tents, beds and arrangements for cooking meals in tamp fashion.
Archbishop O'Doherty of the Philippine Islands went to Mundelein, Illinois, in company with a number of delegates from the Hawaiian Islands and several Spanish American countries. They will prepare for the great Eucharistic procession scheduled to take place in Mundelein on Thursday.

label: text
text: Archbishop O'Doherty Aids.

label: text
text:
The regional meetings which include the group from the countries of Spanish America, the Hawaiian Islands and the Philippines, will concentrate on the study of the spiritual purposes and significance of the Eucharistic Congress. This is in accordance with the plan of having each sectional group choose a special line of study and activity.
Archbishop O'Doherty has been attending most of the Spanish sectional meetings which are held regularly in St. Francis Hall. Cardinal Reig Y. Casanova has been devoting most of his time to the care and assistance of Spanish speaking pilgrims.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHAOS IN CHINA.

label: text
text:
STRONG HINT TO THE POWERS
TO ACT.

label: text
text: The “Times,” “commenting in an editorial headed ‘Ungoverned China.’” emphasises “the lack of Central Government as the root of the trouble, and doubts whether one will emerge from the deliberations of Chang and Wu, and adds that the defence of foreign interests is thus doubly difficult, but that it is an inadequate excuse for inaction. The plundering of revenue and of hypothecated foreign loans cannot be allowed to continue.

label: text
text: The attempt of the Shantung militarists to float a loan and secure the salt revenue is a flagrant violation of the 1913 Reorganisation Loan Agreement.

label: text
text: The "Times" lauds the personality and vigour of the British Consuls who often mitigated the harm done to their countrymen and secured redress, and says, referring to the Customs, that the foreign Powers are not dependent on moral force alone since their fleets ride at anchor in the Treaty Ports, and it does not doubt that if violent hands were laid on the one remaining source of income for the Peking Administration, the Powers would take combined action.

label: text
text: It concludes that whatever the fate of the transient figures composing the Peking Cabinet, the Government, as an institution, remains permanent, and each successive Ministry may properly be invited to assume the obligations of its predecessor; and in case of refusal there is no reason why commitments and promises to the Powers by China should not lapse. The promise of tariff autonomy by 1929 need not necessarily stand if all else fall.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Joseph Scott became famous during the war as a special commander in charge of the field workers of the Knights of Columbus. label: paragraph_title
text: CHINESE RICE FOKIS CATCH IT.

label: text
text: SILKWORMS DIE

label: text
text:
Fakkai, Kongmoon, June 23.
The Canton-Samshui Railway Co. proposes to build a new line from Fatshan to Kongmoon. Engineers have been sent to Kongmoon to survey the land and map out the route.

label: text
text: The silk cocoon market at Pakkai has opened again for the third time this year. Business is very dull. Owing to the recent violent fluctuations in the weather, many silkworms died just before the spinning season.

label: text
text: Rice has gone up 50 cents a picul. This is not due to any shortage in stocks. The "temporary employees" have brought about the "ca' canny" in order that they may find work—as they have been idle for some time—they have insisted that the "permanent employees" (who "are embodied in a guild") should stop work for a time, or, in other words, "reduce hours for their mutual benefit.

label: paragraph_title
text: Current Gossip.

label: text
text: On June 14, the inaugural ceremony was held of the Association (at Canton) of Merchants, Labourers, Peasants and Educators. (Note: It was this body, which recently petitioned the Canton Government to open negotiations to settle the boycott).

label: text
text: Local public opinion is reflected in the following current street gossip. The people are very satisfied with the local militarists! No press gangs are tolerated: Soldiers are ruly and there is no open corruption. The officers are brave and honest. But the Merchants' Protective and Anti-smuggling Bureau is becoming very unpopular. The people call it the Smugglers' Protective and Anti-merchants' Bureau.

label: text

SIXTY MILLION LIRE
INVOLVED.

label: text
text: Much scandal has been caused by the failure of the Banca Agricola of Parma, the sum involved being about sixty million lire.

label: text
text: Twenty-five warrants have been issued, and there have been sixteen arrests, including the Director, Count, Lasignani, who is ex-Mayor of Parma, a professor of Roman laws, a barrister, a politician, and M. Biaggi, the Swiss Consul at Genoa, an ex-director. Lasignani attributes the failure to political enemies.—Reuter.
